commands.summary: decisions/0047-session-scoped-working-tree-rog-overlay-and-dirty-state-contract.md binds: the durable rog/ baseline remains committed and explicit/operator-driven; a working overlay is in-memory, session-scoped, reconstructable, non-authoritative, non-durable; watcher events are invalidation/update hints re-stat'd before being trusted, with explicit conservative-reconciliation fallback rules for directory-shaped/oversized bursts; and basis/coverage/durable-freshness are three orthogonal dimensions, not one flattened enum. Explicitly rejects 'watcher event -> graph.update -> rewrite rog/' as still paying the full projection-walk cost per event while additionally rewriting the committed durable baseline on ordinary edits.

14/14 new overlay tests pass: a single semantic edit (one reparse, unrelated contributions reused, basis becomes working_overlay); a multi-file burst (only touched files reparse); addition/deletion/rename (delete+add, no fabricated identity); an unsupported-file change (inventory updates without fabricating semantics); a parser failure (coverage becomes partial without destroying unrelated contributions) and its recovery; pre-existing dirty state detected at session open with zero watcher history; a directory-level event and an oversized burst both falling back to a full reconcile; a duplicate/no-op watcher event (zero reparse, no generation bump); an explicit refresh reconciling a change the watcher never reported; a 100-file fixture proving exactly one reparse for one changed file; and a dedicated hard test hashing every durable node/edge shard and rog/manifest.json before and after a burst of overlay operations, proving byte-identical durable output throughout.

83/83 total (69 pre-existing unchanged + 14 new), including the ROG-012 equivalence matrix and the WI057 bounded-git-invocation test, confirming the incremental::plan_reconciliation extraction (behavior-preserving refactor backing both graph.update and the overlay) introduced no regression.

14/14 (11 pre-existing unchanged including the two WI057 tests desktop_reads_reuse_one_snapshot_generation_without_git_fanout and watcher_burst_has_one_bounded_refresh_and_ignores_build_churn, + 3 new): a watcher-reported plain source edit updates the graph even though RepositorySnapshot::token() (governance-record content only) never changes -- closing a real pre-existing gap where ordinary source edits never updated the cached graph at all; a self-applied mutation updates the graph immediately (before any watcher poll), with a later watcher report of the same paths recognized as SelfApply rather than duplicated; and ordinary session activity (open, watcher-driven edits, explicit refresh) never creates or writes rog/.
Full workspace green (repopact-graph 83, repopact-desktop-api 14, repopact-validation 49, repopact-mutation 15, all others unaffected).

TypeScript type-checks clean after extending the generated contract (GraphBasis/GraphCoverageState/DurableFreshness/EffectiveGraphStatus, GraphView.status). 16/16 frontend tests pass (14 pre-existing + 2 new proving a working-overlay/partial state and a stale-durable state each render a distinct status line, never flattened into 'current complete').

WSL2 Debian 13 checkout at ~/repopact-linux (never /mnt/c/...) fast-forwarded to this checkpoint's pushed commits and rebuilt; cargo test -p repopact-graph -p repopact-desktop-api and cargo test --workspace both reproduce the exact same pass counts (83/14, full workspace green) as native Windows. No macOS execution occurred or is claimed. The durable graph format itself is unchanged by this checkpoint (no schema-major bump, no new manifest fields), so no new cross-platform byte-equivalence proof was required beyond what ROG-012's checkpoint already established -- this run instead re-proves the overlay engine's own test suite is platform-independent.

commands.command: Real RepoPact-scale engineering performance evidence (engineering validation only, not S8/R1, not claimed toward ROG-032)
commands.summary: On a disposable ~1,470-file copy of RepoPact's own live checkout (via a small standalone harness driving repopact_graph::overlay::SessionGraphState directly, since the overlay is a session/desktop-only primitive with no engine CLI surface): full durable build 3.28s; session open against a fresh durable baseline (loads verbatim, but still pays one projection walk to confirm the fingerprint match per Decision 0047 section 7) 2.63s; a single-file watcher-style update 559ms (1 file reparsed, 696 reused) -- roughly 4-6x faster than a full walk on this fixture, and qualitatively far below the ~21-25s full/incremental durable-operation costs ROG-012 measured on file-count-hashing-dominated repositories; a duplicate/no-op watcher event 294.5 microseconds; a 10-event burst on the same file 541ms total (~54ms/event after the first); a 5-file multi-file burst 683ms; an explicit full session refresh 2.23s (a full projection walk, exactly as intended for the correctness-recovery path). The durable rog/ directory was written exactly once (the initial build) and never touched again by any of the seven subsequent overlay operations, corroborating the dedicated unit-level byte-identical-shards test on real (not synthetic) content.

Both pre-existing repopact-desktop-api WI057 tests (desktop_reads_reuse_one_snapshot_generation_without_git_fanout, watcher_burst_has_one_bounded_refresh_and_ignores_build_churn) pass unchanged. No new Git invocation is added by overlay reconciliation -- delta computation and contribution reuse are pure in-memory/disk-shard operations, never Git calls; the existing bounded RepositorySnapshot cadence (<=4 invocations) is preserved exactly as before this checkpoint.
Dashboard regenerated and committed; canonical repopact validate passes with zero diagnostics on the live (graph-disabled) checkout.

closeout.decision_0047: accepted -- session-scoped, in-memory, non-durable working overlay; watcher events are hints re-stat'd before trust, with explicit directory/burst fallback to a full in-memory reconcile; basis/coverage/durable-freshness kept orthogonal
closeout.overlay_architecture: SessionGraphState (repopact-graph::overlay) owns durable-baseline loading (durable::load_graph, no reparsing when fingerprint matches), an in-memory current_inventory (path->digest) patched incrementally per changed path, a semantic_by_file cache reused across reconcile() calls, and the assembled effective_graph; reconcile(changed_paths) re-stats only the reported paths and regenerates only their semantic contributions via the same semantic::build_file_contribution primitive Decision 0046 established; refresh() performs one full projection walk diffed against the overlay's own current inventory (not the durable baseline) for explicit correctness recovery
closeout.durable_vs_effective_status_model: GraphBasis (durable/working_overlay), GraphCoverageState (complete/partial), and DurableFreshness (absent/fresh/stale/unsupported/corrupt) are three new orthogonal types combined into EffectiveGraphStatus -- status::Freshness (the durable CLI's own model) is untouched
closeout.in_memory_inventory: current_inventory: BTreeMap<String,String> (path -> content digest), seeded once per session-open projection walk, then patched per changed path via Repository::path_state on a targeted re-stat -- never a repeated full projection walk on the watcher-driven hot path
closeout.changed_path_reconciliation: for each watcher-reported path: symlink_metadata classifies it first (absent -> deletion if tracked; directory/symlink -> conservative full-reconcile fallback; regular file -> path_state digest compared against current_inventory, no-op if unchanged, else build_file_contribution and cache update)
closeout.watcher_fallback_rules: a directory-shaped or symlink path in a changed-path set, or a burst exceeding overlay::LARGE_BURST_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD (64), triggers SessionGraphState::refresh (a full in-memory reconcile) rather than a targeted patch; never writes durable state as this fallback
closeout.self_apply_behavior: apply_mutation_plan's success branch calls overlay.reconcile(&snapshot, &changed_paths) using the mutation's own exact changed paths immediately after a successful apply, before any watcher poll; the pre-existing pending_self_paths/ChangeOrigin::SelfApply de-duplication is preserved unchanged, and the overlay's own no-op detection additionally guarantees no duplicate semantic work when the watcher later reports the same paths
closeout.durable_no_write_proof: a dedicated repopact-graph::overlay test hashes rog/manifest.json and every node/edge shard before and after a 5-round burst of reconcile() calls (edit, add, delete) and asserts byte-identical output; corroborated on a real ~1,470-file fixture where the durable directory was written exactly once (the initial build) across seven subsequent overlay operations, and by a dedicated repopact-desktop-api test proving ordinary session activity (open/watcher/refresh) never creates rog/ at all

ac_reassessment.ROG-017: Reassessed, not newly implemented this checkpoint. Direct inspection of Decision 0045 and the semantic-adapter checkpoint's evidence record (20260913-063-semantic-checkpoint) confirms every clause of ROG-017's exact text already has genuine evidence: a language-neutral SemanticAdapter interface (parser-neutral, no Tree-sitter type crosses the boundary); Tree-sitter evaluated against syn/Python-specific/SWC-Oxc alternatives; the selected approach recorded against determinism, incremental capability (evaluated as a selection criterion, not implemented -- ROG-017's text asks only that incremental behavior be part of the evaluation), portability (a real cross-compile spike plus proven Windows/Linux builds), parse safety (malformed-input/cancellation/recursion-bound handling), language coverage (Rust/Python/JS/JSX/TS/TSX), packaging cost (+73.6% binary size, measured), and Rust-core integration (the adapter lives in the canonical repopact-graph crate). Marked satisfied against evidence ID 20260913-063-semantic-checkpoint, not this checkpoint's own evidence -- this working-overlay checkpoint did not implement or modify semantic extraction.

ac_notes.ROG-013: Every required behavior is proven: session-local, non-durable, reconstructable overlay state; watcher events treated as hints and re-verified, never trusted at face value; explicit conservative fallback for directory-level/oversized ambiguity; self-applied mutations reflected immediately; pre-existing dirty state detected without watcher history; durable rog/ never rewritten by ordinary session activity. Marked satisfied.
ac_notes.ROG-010: All six required states (fresh, working-overlay/dirty-aware, partial, stale, unsupported, corrupt) are now real, typed (GraphBasis/GraphCoverageState/DurableFreshness), and disclosed through GraphView.status; a supported client (the desktop Workbench's Graph page status line) renders working-overlay and partial-coverage and stale-durable states distinctly rather than flattening any of them into 'current complete,' proven by two dedicated frontend tests. Marked satisfied.

acs_still_pending.ROG-004/018/022: unchanged disclosed gaps from the semantic-adapter checkpoint (broader edge taxonomy; exported/public detection; JSON/TOML/YAML/Markdown/manifest semantic coverage explicitly named in ROG-018's own text; minified/generated file policy) -- this checkpoint deliberately did not broaden semantic scope or implement additional language adapters.
acs_still_pending.ROG-031: the broad conformance matrix now includes a genuinely proven durable-no-write-during-overlay-use property in addition to the incremental/full equivalence item ROG-012 already proved, but this checkpoint did not audit every remaining item in that matrix (clean clone, symlink/nested-repo boundaries, etc.) as one coordinated pass.
acs_still_pending.ROG-032: engineering performance evidence was gathered for the overlay specifically (session open/reconcile/refresh timings), but the AC's full dedicated benchmark suite (peak memory, local-cache size, clean-clone load time, representative query latency, branch/merge rebuild cost) was not attempted; not claimed.

closeout.python_regression: 285 passed, 2 skipped, 18 subtests passed, 1025.80s (0:17:05); 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this checkpoint (GuardAuthorityTests::test_isolated_self_test_ignores_environment_and_checkout_injection, ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cryptography' under `python -I`) -- the same environment gap already disclosed in the incremental-equivalence checkpoint's evidence record, traced to WI050-era files this checkpoint did not touch; not weakened or worked around.
closeout.next_phase: Two credible options: (a) a persistent Tree-sitter syntax-tree cache / incremental reparse layer on top of the now-proven contribution-reuse overlay, for genuinely large repositories where even single-file reparse cost matters; or (b) closing the disclosed ROG-018/022 semantic-coverage gaps (JSON/TOML/YAML/Markdown adapters, exports detection, minified/generated policy) before adding further overlay sophistication. A fresh architecture review should decide between the two; this checkpoint does not proceed into either.
